column2: 🔴 CANADA HAS NO NATIONAL K-12 AI POSITION AND CANNOT HAVE ONE: K-12 is provincial.  A single "Canada" cell is as wrong as a single "North America" cell was.  The live instruments span a FULL RANGE — Quebec SUSPENDS AI assistants, BC publishes a decision framework, Ontario's ministry is SILENT and its boards and board-IT consortium fill the gap, New Brunswick writes AI INTO THE CURRICULUM.

🟢 So the Canadian engagement unit is the PROVINCE, and in Ontario it is the SCHOOL BOARD.  A product configurable per-province, defaulting to the NARROWEST live rule (Quebec's suspension), satisfies all four; one built to BC's framework fails Quebec.  🔵 Same structure as p377's Norway finding, where Udir bars ACCESS and regjeringen.no bars USE: build the narrower one.

🟢 MEXICO IS PRE-INSTRUMENT AND SAYS SO ITSELF.  There is no binding national rule; there IS a consultation heading for Congress, a UNESCO technical-support agreement, and a measured 76.7 % of public-institution students who do not know whether their own school has guidelines.  🔵 The opportunity is the GOVERNANCE LAYER — policy templates, disclosure workflows, teacher-facing audit trails — not another tutor.  And it is a window that closes when the Congress initiative lands.

🔵 Mexico's higher-education demand is MEASURED (>60 % daily use, SEP's own survey) while its basic-education demand is NOT.  The same split p377 left open for APAC, now recorded for LATAM's largest Spanish-speaking system.

CLOSED.  Canada is placed with four distinct provincial instruments across two languages and Mexico with a dated TIER-1 federal sequence.  Any future "North America" cell on these shelves must name its jurisdiction.

🔴 Quebec's directive was last CONFIRMED in force in December 2025.  Ten months old at this pass, on a TIER-2 outlet, and no 2026 update was found.  A suspension is the strictest fact on the Canadian leg and it is the least currently evidenced.
